newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's grains futures reverse falls on rain.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's grains futures reverse falls on rain.

text.p: Most Hungarian milling wheat futures closed higher on Tuesday in a correction to recent sharp falls and also as a result of concern that too much rain may damage crops, traders said.

Grain futures had fallen sharply recently as a rainy period followed weeks of unseasonally hot, dry weather. More rain than usual is also forecast for the first 10 days of June and this may harm crops, traders said.
"If it rains too much, the wheat may be beaten down," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex Rt.
Traders said two of the main market players appeared as buyers on Tuesday, while the third was taking a wait-and-see stance.
Price trends on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) grain section will be determined by news about weather and world market prices, traders said.
"If the falling trend in Chicago reverses, we will be going up too," Szoke said.
BCE grains futures turnover rose to 455.6 million forints on Tuesday from 380.2 million Monday.
